description: Offline forward and reverse geocoder: one memory-mapped file per country, with Python, CLI, DuckDB and MCP interfaces. No server, no API key.
rules: Install with `pip install gridpin gridpin-mcp`; download a country sheet with `gridpin-fetch <code>` (us, de, fr, it, es, nl, br, rs) or `gridpin_mcp.sheets.download(code)`, which verifies it against the signed release and returns its path.
One sheet holds one country: open `gridpin.Geocoder(path)` for the country of the address; other countries are not covered, and Germany has no Bavaria.
Check `precision` in every result: `house` is a door-level match, `street` and `city` are approximate; reverse geocoding returns `distance_m` and is approximate.
For many addresses use `Geocoder.geocode_many(queries, k)` in Python or `gridpin batch` in the CLI instead of a loop of single calls.

In DuckDB 1.5.6+ (older DuckDB versions install an older build): `INSTALL gridpin_ext FROM community; LOAD gridpin_ext;`, then `SELECT gridpin_load(path)` once per session; one country per session, `SELECT gridpin_reset()` to switch.
Geocoding never uses the network; only downloading a sheet does.
